rv.q: Faithful readers will note that I’ve been doling out positive reviews left and right these days. That speaks to the general high quality of Broadway as of late; I cannot recall the last production I saw that wasn’t at least decent.

Youth isn’t only for the young, at least not as a marketable commodity in popular entertainment. On Broadway as in Hollywood, there will always be generation-crossing shows displaying fresh-fleshed things in hormonally induced states of agony and ecstasy.
13 is a show that knows exactly what it wants to be and exactly how to be it, even if what it wants to be isn't necessarily groundbreaking or sophisticated.
Wright furiously tears around as the flamboyant Jacques.

cn.t: Critics find this all-teen musical energetic but uneven, with some charmed by its youthful exuberance while others see it as a calculated commercial venture that doesn't deliver a truly memorable theatrical experience.
